source_read: PMC HTML (PMC6729247; J Neurosci 2004;24:6028-6036): abstract, Introduction, Materials and Methods (participants, Tables 1-3, drug use, neuropsychological testing, mood, MRI acquisition, image processing, cortical pattern matching, hippocampal maps), Results (cortical maps, hippocampal deficits, whole-brain measures, lateralization), Figure 1-4 legends, Discussion (incl. significance maps, cortical pattern matching, limitations), funding footnote.

claims.overstatement: The magnitude 'cingulate-paralimbic grey matter -11.3%' follows the abstract but generalizes beyond the Results: the 11.3% is grey-matter DENSITY (proportion of grey matter in 15-mm spheres) in the RIGHT cingulate gyrus; the left cingulate was 0.7% lower (p=0.4), medial frontal cortex 3.6% (trend, p<0.1), lateral surfaces showed no significant differences, and total grey matter did not differ (p>0.1). Should read 'right cingulate grey-matter density -11.3%'.
claims.note: Confirmed from this source: 22 users vs 21 controls; hippocampal volume -7.8% (p<0.01); white matter +7.0% (p<0.01); no between-group comparison of memory scores is reported anywhere in the paper (only correlations of hippocampal measures with word recall; three other memory measures did not correlate). Not checkable here: the later non-replication by the same laboratory and the smoking-stratified study (other sources). This study had 15/22 tobacco smokers among users vs 2/21 controls and a 2.4-year education gap, neither adjusted.

anchors.locator: Results > Mapping cortical gray-matter deficits; Lateralization of cingulate deficits; Figure 1 and Figure 3e legends
anchors.extracted: Cortical pattern-matching maps of grey-matter density: significant deficit in a cingulate/subgenual/paralimbic belt (permutation-corrected p<0.05; legend p<0.034). Right cingulate density 11.3% below controls; left cingulate 0.7% (p=0.4); adjacent medial frontal 3.6% (p<0.1); left medial wall and both lateral surfaces not significant after correction. Users lose the normal right>left cingulate asymmetry.

anchors.locator: Results > Hippocampal deficits; Figure 3a and Figure 4 legends
anchors.extracted: Hippocampal volume 7.8% smaller in users (p<0.01); left -8.2% (p=0.01), right -7.5% (p<0.05) in regressions adjusting for age and sex; held after adjusting for brain size and after excluding 6 heavy cannabis users. Total and right hippocampal volume correlated with word recall (p<0.05); left radial atrophy related to group (p<0.05) and word recall (p=0.01; p<0.05 Bonferroni for 4 tests). Picture recall, word and picture recognition did not correlate. No group means or group test for any memory score are reported; whether correlations were pooled across groups is not stated.

anchors.locator: Results > Whole-brain gray- and white-matter measures
anchors.extracted: No group difference in total cerebral volume or total grey matter (p>0.1). Total white matter 7.0% greater in users (p<0.01): left +6.6% (p=0.01), right +7.5% (p<0.01); temporal and occipital white matter larger; right frontal horn of lateral ventricle 25.2% larger (p<0.05).

anchors.locator: Materials and Methods > Participants, Table 1, Table 2; Discussion, limitations paragraph
anchors.extracted: Users 15 men/7 women, controls 10/11; education 12.8 vs 15.2 years (p<0.001); tobacco >5 cigarettes/day 15/22 vs 2/21; cannabis days 2.38 vs 0.14 in past 30. Authors name the smoking imbalance as a limitation and argue that smoking-related grey-matter differences reported elsewhere were more restricted and did not involve the hippocampus. Neither smoking nor education is adjusted in the analyses.

key_findings.correction: The 11.3% is the mean grey-matter density reduction in the RIGHT cingulate gyrus (Lateralization of cingulate deficits; Figure 3e legend), not a figure for the whole cingulate/subgenual/paralimbic region. The broader region is where the permutation-corrected map was significant; no single percentage is given for it. Suggested wording: 'Right cingulate grey-matter density 11.3% lower; the corrected cortical map showed a deficit across a cingulate, subgenual and paralimbic belt on the right medial surface.'

Drop 'by self-report': the paper gives abstinence only as 'mean days abstinent 6.64 (SD 5.2)' in Table 3 and does not say how it was established or verified (as the card's own exposure field notes). All other figures confirmed.
Recomputed: education g about 1.12, Beck Depression Inventory about 1.14, age about 0.47.

reporting_issues.note: Not an inconsistency: p<0.034 satisfies p<0.05, and p=0.4 satisfies p>0.1. The reporting is imprecise (different levels of precision for the same tests) but not contradictory; suggest deleting or rewording as 'reported at different precision'.
Recomputed from means and SEMs: t about 1.44, p about 0.16.

Recomputed treating parentheses as SEM (Table 3 footnote a): trait t about 1.91, p about 0.07; state t about 1.58, p about 0.13. Treating them as SDs would make trait p<0.001 but state p<0.001 too, so no single reading reproduces both printed values; the BDI value (p<0.0005) reproduces only with SEMs.
The 'volume' wording is in the Results (Mapping cortical gray-matter deficits) and the Figure 1 legend; the abstract says 'gray-matter deficits', not 'volume'.
Found independently in step 1 (time from last use to MRI not stated).

risk_of_bias.note: Agree that overall risk of bias is high, but the labels are inconsistent: 'serious' is a ROBINS-I category, not ROBINS-E (low / some concerns / high / very high), and with three domains rated 'high' the ROBINS-E overall judgment should be at least 'high', not 'serious'. 'Measurement of the exposure: high' looks too severe for a SCID-diagnosed dependent group compared with screened non-users (misclassification of the binary exposure is unlikely; 'some concerns' for the unverified recency of use).

interpretation_gap.note: Severe: the abstract states that use 'causes' deterioration that 'contributes to impaired memory performance' although the design is cross-sectional and no group memory comparison is reported.

missed: Whether the hippocampal volume-word recall correlations were computed across both groups pooled or within the methamphetamine group is not stated (Results > Hippocampal deficits); if pooled, the correlation partly restates the group difference and is open to the same confounders (education, smoking). The card's 'within the sample' wording leaves this open.
For cl_meth_grey_matter: the claim's magnitude 'cingulate-paralimbic grey matter -11.3%' inherits the abstract's generalization; the Results restrict the 11.3% to right cingulate density.
